title: imap: IMAP4rev2 support (RFC 9051)
description:
Support IMAP4rev2 alongside IMAP4rev1. RFC 9051 is the successor to RFC 3501 and absorbs many extensions as mandatory baseline.

Extensions folded into IMAP4rev2 that are already tracked as separate issues here: IDLE, MOVE, UNSELECT, ENABLE, LITERAL+, SPECIAL-USE, CONDSTORE (partial), LIST-EXTENDED, LIST-STATUS, SEARCHRES, ID.

Additional IMAP4rev2 requirements beyond IMAP4rev1:
- NAMESPACE (RFC 2342): mailbox namespace prefixes; required by RFC 9051.
- STATUS=SIZE (RFC 8438): mailbox size in octets in STATUS responses.
- FETCH SAVEDATE: message save date distinct from internal date.
- Stricter UTF-8 handling throughout (RFC 9051 requires UTF-8 in more places than RFC 3501).
- SASL-IR (RFC 4959): initial client response in AUTHENTICATE; reduces round-trips for AUTH=PLAIN.

Approach: advertise both IMAP4rev1 and IMAP4rev2 in CAPABILITY. When a client sends ENABLE IMAP4rev2, activate RFC 9051 semantics for that session. imap-codec already models IMAP4rev2 types.
notes: Capability::Other(CapabilityOther) is the escape hatch — use Capability::try_from("IMAP4REV2") to advertise today without waiting on upstream. When imap-types ships Capability::Imap4Rev2 (duesee/imap-codec#702), swap the one line. This issue is no longer blocked.
